# Architecture

`ms-go-statistic` collects fine-grained coding telemetry and derives per-user task summaries. It owns accepted telemetry rows and the summary projection, but not identities, courses, lessons, tasks, sessions, progress, or authorization policy.

The service follows a ports-and-adapters split: `internal/domain` defines events, summaries, and repository ports; `internal/usecase` validates and orchestrates ingestion/queries through ports; `internal/transport/http/api` owns public HTTP and WebSocket delivery while `internal/transport/http/private` owns internal-only delivery; `internal/infrastructure/persistence/clickhouse` buffers, persists, and queries rows; `internal/infrastructure/messaging/nats` publishes observations. `cmd/ms-go-statistic/main.go` is the composition root.

Both transports trust `X-User-Id` and `X-User-Role` supplied by an upstream gateway. The role is recorded but does not authorize operations. Summary queries always filter by the supplied user UUID. Consequently, direct untrusted access to the service permits identity spoofing.

The API accepts opaque course, lesson, task, and session UUIDs without synchronous ownership or existence checks. The service must not introduce foreign ownership rules locally; stronger authorization belongs at the trusted integration boundary.

The service derives bounded active-learning summaries without owning the
Student `LearningSession`. It may publish an observational interesting-activity
event after cheap analysis. `ms-go-teacher-agent` decides whether to intervene;
`ms-go-student` remains the owner of session and learning state.
